guard: the Hermes sidecar's auto-injected turn cannot be framed by a peer: the body, the sender name and role, and the kind rendered beside them all pass through one neutralization, and the pre-fix concatenation is re-measured as a refuse control on every run
why: The Python sidecar built the injected turn by concatenation, `"[<kind> from {fromName}] " + text`,
both fields raw, so it carried the same two forgeries the TypeScript formatter did. A body with a
newline wrote a second attribution line, reading as a delivered message from a peer that never
sent one; a sender naming itself with a closing bracket ended the real attribution and opened a
forged one. The text is auto-injected into a turn rather than returned when the model asks.
The mutations are the ways the repair can be undone, one per part of it: the body indent (M1),
the attribution class (M2), and the breadth of what counts as a line break (M3). M1 and M2 are
the half-fixes, each of which leaves the frame forgeable while reading as repaired.
M4 IS DEFENCE IN DEPTH AND IS LABELLED AS SUCH. `kind` is rendered outside the body, so the
positional rule covers it, but every path that reaches this bridge derives it from the subject
the message arrived on rather than from the payload, so no peer sets it today. It was found by
mutating the field and watching the mutation SURVIVE: the neutralization was there and nothing
graded it. The honest options were to delete the line or to pin it; it is pinned, because the
rule is stated absolutely and a renderer whose guarantee holds only while an upstream path keeps
deriving one field correctly is a renderer whose guarantee is somebody else's. The cell names it
as defence in depth so a reader is not told a live hole was closed.
SPECIFIER BOUNDARY, checked rather than assumed. The suite runs the REAL adapter in a Python
subprocess reading `plugin/` by path, so the bytes mutated are the bytes graded: no dist in the
path and no build in the command. Only the upstream `gateway` package is stubbed, because it is
not installed in CI; the adapter, its framing module, and the attribution it builds are the
connector's own real code.

mutations.name: M1 the half-fix: attribution neutralized, the body left to write its own lines
mutations.find: return _LINE_BREAK.sub("\n  ", "" if text is None else str(text))
mutations.replace: return "" if text is None else str(text)
mutations.cell: a message body cannot add an injected line (body_newline)
mutations.expectRed: a message body cannot add an injected line (body_newline)
mutations.note: The indent is the only thing separating what the connector said from what a peer said it said, so an attribution that is safe on its own still leaves the frame forgeable. This is the shape of a fix that reads as complete and closes half the class.

mutations.name: M2 a peer may reach the brackets it is rendered inside
mutations.find: return _UNSAFE_IN_ATTRIBUTION.sub(" ", "" if value is None else str(value))
mutations.replace: return "" if value is None else str(value)
mutations.cell: a peer cannot open a second attribution (name_bracket)
mutations.expectRed: a peer cannot open a second attribution (name_bracket)
mutations.note: The name half of the defect. The attribution is one bracket pair, the one the adapter wrote, so a peer that reached either bracket shows up as a second of one of them.

mutations.name: M3 the break class narrows to what one language's splitlines knows
mutations.cell: a message body cannot add an injected line (body_u2028)
mutations.expectRed: a message body cannot add an injected line (body_u2028)
mutations.note: U+2028, U+2029 and U+0085 survive JSON transport intact into the bytes a model is handed. A rule enforced only against the separators one splitter honours is a rule whose truth depends on which reader is looking, and this rule is stated absolutely. Kept to the same class as the TypeScript side on purpose: a peer that can forge the frame on either side of the socket has the whole class back.

mutations.name: M4 the kind rendered beside the sender is passed through raw (defence in depth)
mutations.cell: a message kind cannot open a second attribution, defence in depth (kind_bracket)
mutations.expectRed: a message kind cannot open a second attribution, defence in depth (kind_bracket)
mutations.note: NOT A LIVE HOLE, and the cell says so. `kind` is subject-derived on every path that reaches this bridge, so no peer sets it today. This mutation exists because an earlier run of it SURVIVED: the neutralization was present and ungraded, which is untested code rather than a caught defect. Pinned rather than deleted, because the positional rule is stated absolutely.
